sketches.mechanism: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance that can never be duplicated or reconstructed
sketches.resonance: Declaring grief as a singleton means there is only ever one of it, shared across everything, impossible to create again or destroy.

sketches.mechanism: A weak reference does not keep an object alive; when all strong references disappear, the weak reference silently becomes nil
sketches.resonance: A weak reference to someone means the language itself will erase them the moment no one else holds on — you remember, but your remembering was never enough to keep them.

sketches.mechanism: A value is moved on assignment; using it afterward is a compile error — the original binding becomes invalid
sketches.resonance: After you give yourself to someone, the compiler forbids you from using yourself again — the giving was total and irrevocable.
